w10_T4_009030: A restaurant chain had 113 tables. They subtracted 71 tables after closing a location. Then added 73 tables when opening a new branch. They added 27 more tables during expansion. w10_T4_009040: A warehouse started with 113 inventory items. They subtracted 22 items sold. Then removed 34 more damaged items. They removed another 14 items for replacement. w10_T4_009046: A farm had 228 acres. They doubled the planted area. Then divided by 6 to allocate between crops. They divided by 2 again for separate sections. Then added 60 acres for pasture. w10_T4_009054: A manufacturer had 63 units. They doubled production. Then multiplied by 6 for the factory run. They added 8 units from a special order. w10_T4_009060: A clinic had 143 patient files. They added 48 new patient files. Then added 50 more from a satellite office. They subtracted 60 files that were archived. w10_T4_009065: A storage facility had 206 units. They multiplied by 8 when organizing inventory. Then by 4 for a full account. They added 64 units from new acquisitions. w10_T4_009066: A logistics company had 201 shipments. They multiplied by 7 for weekly tracking. Then by 8 for a full network. They divided by 4 to allocate to regions. w10_T4_009068: A library started with 60 reference books. They subtracted 10 old editions. Then added 12 new reference books. They added 35 more from a donation. w10_T4_009072: A farm had 56 harvest baskets. They added 46 baskets. Then multiplied by 4 for the full harvest. They subtracted 19 damaged baskets. w10_T4_009092: A company had 134 work orders. They multiplied by 3 for a three-month projection. They subtracted 39 orders that were cancelled. Then added 76 new orders. Finally, 50 more orders came in. Tracking these changes along with project milestones, how many orders is the company managing?
w10_T4_009095: A delivery service started with 49 packages. In the morning, they added 7 packages. Then removed 10 packages at a stop. They added 79 packages at the depot. w10_T4_009100: A school had 34 desks. They subtracted 1 broken desk. Then added 73 new desks. They subtracted 7 desks for repairs. Then added 79 more desks. w10_T4_009101: A supplier had 201 items. They added 27 items in a restock. They divided by 2 for two location assignments. They subtracted 40 items sold. w10_T4_009102: A bakery started with 158 pastries. They added 6 items from a special order. They doubled them for the display. Then added 16 more pastries. Finally, 37 more items arrived. Using the word 'triple', how many pastries does the bakery have after morning production?
w10_T4_009112: A gym had 85 member files. They subtracted 77 inactive members. They multiplied by 9 for a membership projection. They subtracted 16 for cancellations. w10_T4_009116: A factory had 118 units. They multiplied by 9 for production. They subtracted 337 units due to defects. They multiplied by 5 for a week's output. Then by 5 again for monthly planning. w10_T4_009124: A warehouse had 150 items. They multiplied by 9 in the morning phase. Then by 6 for the afternoon phase. They added 79 new items. They subtracted 5223 items due to a major recall. w10_T4_009139: A farmer started with 50 apples in the morning. They added 5 more apples. Then 57 more from a second tree. They added 46 from a third tree. They subtracted 15 apples sold at market. w10_T4_009143: A printing company had 158 jobs. They multiplied by 7 for project tracking. They added 65 more jobs. They multiplied by 3 for a quarterly estimate. They subtracted 910 completed jobs. w10_T4_009151: A school started with 25 students. They added 62 students in morning enrollment. They multiplied by 3 for a classroom projection. Then by 8 to account for all grades. w10_T4_009152: A store had 59 items. They multiplied by 5 for the weekly inventory. Then by 4 for the monthly count. Then by 4 again for quarterly planning. They added 68 items from restocking. w10_T4_009153: A project had 151 tasks. They subtracted 61 completed tasks. Then added 7 newly identified tasks. They added 54 more tasks. They multiplied by 4 for a tracking system. w10_T4_009159: A bakery had 50 batches. They multiplied by 3 for morning production. Then by 7 for daily total. They added 15 more batches. They multiplied by 4 for a week's projection. w10_T4_009161: A logistics hub had 238 packages. They multiplied by 9 for initial sorting. Then by 3 for regional distribution. Then by 3 for sub-regional sorting. w10_T4_009163: A factory had 62 units. They multiplied by 7 for the shift. They added 35 units from the previous shift. They added 71 more in the overnight batch.
